questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help prevent a truck from rolling over?

options.text: Keeping cargo as low as possible
Driving on the shoulder of a road

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving on the shoulder of a road
questions.explanation: To prevent a truck from rolling over, keep cargo weight as low as possible and drive slowly around turns. Driving on the shoulder does not help prevent rollovers.

questions.question: If you double your speed from 20 mph to 40 mph, how does this affect braking distance?
questions.explanation: When you double your speed from 20 to 40 mph, your braking distance becomes four times longer. Higher speeds increase both the truck's power and the distance needed to stop.

questions.question: If a tire fails, you should:
questions.explanation: Using brakes after a tire fails can cause you to lose control. Avoid braking until your vehicle has slowed down significantly.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Only use the driver's side mirror

questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Check both mirrors frequently and use a helper whenever possible.

questions.question: One way to prevent fatigue on long trips is to:
questions.explanation: Take a break every 100 miles or every 2 hours. Driving when you would normally be sleeping increases the risk of fatigue.

questions.question: When starting a vehicle, the oil pressure should:

options.text: Gradually build up over a few minutes
Reach normal within a few seconds
Start high, then decrease as the engine runs

questions.correctAnswerText: Reach normal within a few seconds
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should reach normal levels within seconds of starting the engine.

questions.question: The best way to know your trailer has started to skid is by:

options.text: Watching the trailer in your mirrors

questions.correctAnswerText: Watching the trailer in your mirrors
questions.explanation: Looking at your mirrors is the best way to see a trailer skid early. You can spot the problem as soon as it starts.

questions.question: If your brakes fail while going downhill and there is no escape ramp, you should:
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail and there is no escape ramp, look for a safe place to stop. This could be an open field or a road that is flat or goes uphill.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not apply brakes if the vehicle is out of gear

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. Chock the wheels if needed.

questions.question: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the highest safe temperature, you should:

options.text: Pull over and check what's wrong

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check what's wrong
questions.explanation: Stop driving immediately if the coolant temperature is too high. A problem with your engine could cause failure or fire.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should check your mirrors:
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. Check them even more often when you change lanes.

questions.question: Which is NOT a recommended way to spot vehicle problems?

options.text: Watch the gauges on the instrument panel.
Use your senses to notice problems.
Check important items only at the start and end of a trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check important items only at the start and end of a trip.
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle regularly during the trip, not just at the beginning and end. Look at gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights. Use all your senses to catch problems early.

questions.question: Heights posted at bridges:
questions.explanation: Do not assume a posted bridge height is correct. Road changes like repaving or snow can affect clearance. Always be careful.

questions.question: Black ice is usually:
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. It looks like wet pavement. Watch for it when the road appears wet but the temperature is below freezing.

questions.question: One way to prevent hydroplaning on wet roads is to:

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
Let air out of your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your tires with good tread depth.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens more easily when tire pressure is low or tread is worn. If hydroplaning starts, release the accelerator and slow down.

questions.question: When going downhill, your vehicle will:

options.text: Stay at the same speed as level roads.

questions.explanation: Gravity pulls your vehicle faster when going downhill. Slow down before you reach a downgrade.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system can:

options.text: Allow poisonous fumes into the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow poisonous fumes into the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. Poisonous fumes can enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: If you do not drain air tanks, what could happen?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brakes to fail.
Too much air collects in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brakes to fail.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and oil. If water is not removed, it can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure.

questions.question: Having anti-lock brakes on only one axle will:

options.text: Give you better control when braking.
Cause the air brakes to break.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you better control when braking.
questions.explanation: Even anti-lock brakes on one axle give you more control than no anti-lock brakes at all.

questions.question: The emergency air line supplies air to the:
questions.explanation: The emergency air line (supply line) does two things. It supplies air to trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.
